title: Add feature flags + cohort assignment for lifecycle growth experiments (email + console) w/ holdout
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Internal-only: introduces lifecycle growth flagging + deterministic cohort assignment (including holdout) for onboarding email and console nudge experiments; no user-visible changes without flags enabled.
body: ## Summary This PR introduces a small, shared experimentation/flagging layer for the lifecycle growth sprint (Hosted API activation/retention). It adds: (1) canonical feature flags for email + console onboarding experiments, (2) deterministic cohort assignment with a configurable holdout group, and (3) guardrails for eligibility + overrides so we can run clean A/B / holdout measurements without re-randomizing users across surfaces. ## Why We currently have separate targeting logic in the email send pipeline and in the Console nudge framework. That makes it easy to accidentally run mismatched cohorts (email sees user in Variant A, console sees same user in control), and it also makes it hard to maintain a stable holdout group for measurement. This PR centralizes cohort assignment and exposes it in a way that both services can consume. ## What’s included - New flag namespace: `lifecycle_growth.*` - Deterministic cohort assignment based on stable identifiers (prefers `workspace_id`, falls back to `user_id`, then `email_hash`), using a salted hash + modulo - Support for holdout cohort (default 10%) that is excluded from all lifecycle_growth experiments by default - Experiment-specific splits (e.g., 50/50 A/B within eligible non-holdout) - Explicit eligibility checks to prevent targeting: (a) users with `email_unsubscribed=true` for email experiments, (b) accounts marked `sales_assisted=true` or `active_opportunity=true` (if present) for retargeting-related flags (stubbed for now; consumed in a follow-up PR), (c) internal @redwoodinference.com dogfood is allowed but tagged - Overrides: admin-only header `X-Experiment-Override` (Console + internal tools) and server-side `experiment_overrides` table for debugging (requires elevated role) - Emits a single, consistent analytics event on cohort assignment: `lifecycle_experiment_assigned` with properties: `experiment_key`, `cohort`, `assignment_id`, `is_holdout`, `assignment_source` ## Flag / experiment keys (initial set) - `lifecycle_growth.email_onboarding_v2` (A/B, gated; holdout excluded) - `lifecycle_growth.console_nudges_v1` (A/B, gated; holdout excluded) - `lifecycle_growth.console_checklist_v0` (off by default; reserved) Note: these flags default to OFF globally. Activation is via env-configured allowlist + cohort system. ## Implementation details - Core logic lives in `packages/experiments/assignment.ts` (shared between console + lifecycle worker) - Salt is configured via `EXPERIMENT_ASSIGNMENT_SALT` and must be set in all envs. If missing, we hard-fail in prod and soft-fail (warn + assign control) in dev/test. - Assignment is idempotent and stable across time as long as the stable ID and salt are unchanged. - Holdout is implemented as a top-level cohort (`holdout`) which short-circuits other experiments under the `lifecycle_growth` namespace. This keeps analytics interpretation simple. - We intentionally log cohort assignment once per (experiment_key, stable_id) per 30 days to reduce event volume. (Can be adjusted.) ## Testing - Unit tests for hashing stability, splits, holdout behavior, and override parsing - Integration tests for Console request path (cohort evaluation + analytics emission) - Added a small fixture to validate that old “random” assignment does not leak into this path ## Rollout plan - Merge behind flags (default OFF) - Stage: enable for dogfood cohort only (internal + a small allowlist) - Production: ramp by increasing eligibility allowlist (not changing split algorithm) - If metrics anomalies occur, disable by setting `LIFECYCLE_GROWTH_EXPERIMENTS_ENABLED=false` (all experiments become control; holdout remains tagged if previously assigned) ## Screenshots / UX None (backend + shared library changes only). ## Checklist - [x] Security/privacy review for stable IDs + hashing (no raw emails in assignment) - [x] Confirmed unsubscribe is respected in email experiment path (gates eligibility) - [x] Added docs in `docs/internal/experiments.md` - [x] Added metric event (`lifecycle_experiment_assigned`) to data catalog stub (follow-up for full schema validation) Related: ENG-10501, PM-663, PM-659
commits: feat(experiments): add deterministic cohort assignment + holdout support
feat(flags): add lifecycle_growth flag namespace and default config
feat(console): wire cohort evaluation into nudge targeting context
feat(lifecycle-worker): gate email onboarding v2 sends behind experiment assignment
test: add unit + integration coverage for assignment stability and overrides
docs: internal write-up for lifecycle_growth experiments and rollout knobs
review_conversation: Jada Williams (review): Can we guarantee stable assignment across email + console if the stable_id differs (user vs workspace)? I’d prefer we always use workspace when available so variants don’t drift as members join/leave.

Ethan Park (author): Yep — updated precedence to `workspace_id` > `user_id` > `email_hash`. Added a test ensuring a user moving between workspaces reassigns (expected) but remains stable within a workspace.

Dylan Brooks (review): Holdout short-circuit is the right idea, but please make sure console doesn’t show the nudge if a user is in holdout even when someone manually enables the flag. Also, where is the switch to fully disable the system in prod if we see anomalies?

Ethan Park (author): Added `is_holdout` check at the experiment gate layer (before any per-experiment cohorting) and a top-level env kill switch `LIFECYCLE_GROWTH_EXPERIMENTS_ENABLED`. Updated docs with rollback instructions.

Nadia Rahman (review): The analytics event name is good. Two requests: (1) include `assignment_id` so we can join/dedupe reliably, and (2) confirm we’re not emitting raw email. We should only send hashed identifiers, if any.

Ethan Park (author): Added `assignment_id` (stable hash of experiment_key + stable_id + salt) and verified no raw email is emitted. The payload only includes experiment_key/cohort/is_holdout plus assignment_id; stable_id never leaves the service boundary.

Michael Grant (privacy review): Please document the retention expectations for assignment logs and ensure overrides are admin-only. Also, in dev, avoid defaulting to random behavior—control is safer for testing if salt is missing.

Ethan Park (author): Overrides are now gated behind `admin:experiments` permission and an allowlisted internal header (only accepted from internal proxy). If salt is missing, we warn and return control in dev/test; in prod we throw at boot. Added notes to docs.
Jada Williams (approval): Approved after the workspace precedence + assignment_id changes.
Dylan Brooks (approval): Looks good. Please follow up with console UI wiring in the nudge PR if anything diverges.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved with the event properties update.
